summary: Bilateral diagnostic fixture for the curl glob_set switch-expression (int*) cast churn. Seven synthetic IR/CFG/type states (aligned, pa_out_int8, pa_in_churn, pa_both_churn, ia_token, cast_chain, globform) are seeded identically on both sides and run through the real ActionSetCasts::apply; each op's inputs/outputs (varnode + high, read-facing), TypeOp output token, apply-side output token, PTRSUB/PTRADD slot-0 input cast, the post-apply op graph with inserted CASTs, the count delta, and (globform) the rendered switch-expression tree are dumped. The pre-stage seeds and globform swexpr_pre are byte-identical; all 13 changed records are the registered known_raw_differences below. This is phase A: the fixture locks the divergence, no src fix is claimed.

function_scope.ghidra_signature: Datatype *TypeOpPtrsub::getInputCast(const PcodeOp *op,int4 slot,const CastStrategy *castStrategy) const [typeop.cc:2320] (and TypeOpPtradd::getInputCast typeop.cc:2250)

known_raw_differences.cause: mult token=int8 vs oracle unknown8: Ghidra TypeOpIntMult::getOutputToken -> CastStrategyC::arithmeticOutputStandard (typeop.cc:1628, cast.cc:394) keeps the max typeOrder input high metatype (unknown8 stays unknown8); Rugra has no TypeOp INT_* token impl, fixture mirrors the apply-side base-int token (coreaction.rs output_metatype). pa atok=null vs oracle ptr8w1->int4: documents that Rugra cast_output skips PTRADD (output_metatype None) while Ghidra coreaction.cc:2541 consumes TypeOpPtradd::getOutputToken (typeop.cc:2244 = in0 high read-facing). Behaviorally neutral in this case (aligned post identical).
same mult token and pa atok field divergences as aligned|pre. pa out high is int8 here, so the oracle token (ptr8w1->int4 = in0 high) differs from out high: castOutput will fire on the oracle side.

FIRST BEHAVIORAL DIVERGENCE. Oracle count=1: castOutput(pa) with token ptr8w1->int4 (TypeOpPtradd::getOutputToken, typeop.cc:2244) vs out high int8 -> implied arm (coreaction.cc:2569-2571) retypes the implied PTRADD output in place to the token (updateType) and inserts CAST(int8) AFTER the ptradd (cc:2595-2609 rewiring: pa->new int8 vn, CAST out = old outvn). Rugra count=0: cast_output has no PTRADD arm (output_metatype None) so nothing happens; pa out stays int8, no CAST.
same mult token / pa atok field divergences; the ic0=ptr8w1->int4 slot-0 input cast (typeop.cc:2250-2263) MATCHES on both sides (seed state identical).
same mult token / pa atok field divergences.

Oracle count=2: input CAST(ptr8w1->int4)(gB) before the ptradd (both sides do this, identical) PLUS castOutput: implied ptradd output retyped to token ptr8w1->int4 in place and CAST(int8) inserted after (the formal nested (T)(T) shape). Rugra count=1: only the input cast; ptradd output stays int8 and no output CAST (missing PTRADD castOutput arm).

INT_ADD token: oracle int8 (TypeOpIntAdd::getOutputToken typeop.cc:1175 -> arithmeticOutputStandard cast.cc:394: max typeOrder over INPUT read-facing highs; bool demoted to int) vs Rugra ptr8w1->int4 (Rust TypeOpIntAdd::get_output_token returns the OUTPUT high instead of the arithmetic standard of the inputs). atok (apply side) matches at int8 by coincidence of the base-int fallback.

Final op graphs are textually IDENTICAL (ia implied int8 + CAST(ptr8w1->int4)); oracle count=2 vs Rugra count=1. The missing +1 is the constant slot: oracle castInput slot1 gets ct from TypeOp::getInputCast (typeop.cc:295: castStandard(inputTypeLocal=int8, const high unknown8) -> non-null) and the constant arm (cc:2687-2691) updateTypes the constant to int8 and returns 1; Rugra's cast_input returns no ct for the INT_ADD constant slot so no count unit. The retyped constant is invisible in the dump (constants print as c#offset).

cast0 atok: oracle prints unknown8 (TypeOpCast token via base getOutputToken -> outputTypeLocal) while the Rust fixture prints na because CAST ops never reach cast_output on the apply side (both Ghidra apply at cc:2739 and Rugra apply skip CPUI_CAST; the oracle field is the never-consumed virtual value, the Rust field documents the skip). mult token int8 vs oracle ptr8w1->int4: arithmeticOutputStandard picks the ptr input high as the max typeOrder type.

MISSING DOUBLE-CAST GUARD. Oracle: castInput(mult,0) sees the input is an implied CAST output with loneDescend==mult -> retypes the existing CAST output IN PLACE to ct=int8 (cc:2673-2679: vn->updateType(ct); if type==ct return 1) and mult keeps reading cast0_o; count=2 (retype + const slot unit). Rugra: stacks a SECOND CAST(int8) on top of the existing CAST(ptr8w1->int4) -> renders as the (int8)(int8*) churn nesting; count=1. This is a direct churn generator: every re-cast of an already-cast expression nests instead of retyping.

mult token (arithmeticOutputStandard unknown8 vs base-int int8), pa atok (PTRADD arm skipped), and ia token (out-high unknown8 vs arithmetic max ptr8w1->int4). The full seed state (types, highs, ic0s, load token, ps token) otherwise matches; swexpr_pre is byte-identical.

EARLIEST apply-step divergence inside globform: the PTRADD fit preflight (cc:2740-2746) fires on the oracle BEFORE pa's input casts - in0 high ptr8w1->int8 has ptrTo alignSize 8 != addressToByteInt(4,1)=4 -> Funcdata::opUndoPtradd(pa,true) (funcdata_op.cc:579) rewrites pa to INT_ADD and inserts the implied INT_MULT scale op (n2, out typed from multVn, inserted before pa). Oracle then inserts int8 input CASTs on both new INT_ADD arms (n3 on ps_o, n4 on the scale-mult out) and the CAST(ptr8w1->int8) after pa (n8). count=7. Rugra has no preflight and no opUndoPtradd: pa stays PTRADD, no scale mult, no int8 input casts, no output CAST; count=4. The load/ia-level casts (ptr8w1->int4 after load, int8 on load_o, int8 on gA) MATCH on both sides, as does the ps output cast n0 (the landed TypeOpPtrsub cast_output arm behaves identically to oracle here).

Rendered switch-expression tree divergence caused entirely by the globform|post op-graph divergence: oracle '((int8)(ptr8w1->int4)*((ptr8w1->int8)((int8)(ptr8w1->int8)PTRSUB(gs,#0) + (int8)((SEXT(idx) * #4) * #4))) + (int8)gA)' vs Rugra '((int8)(ptr8w1->int4)*(((ptr8w1->int8)PTRSUB(gs,#0) + (SEXT(idx) * #4))) + (int8)gA)'. The oracle form is the same mechanical (T)(T) nesting the production glob_set switch exhibits; Rugra's flatter form here is the absence of the undo-ptradd rewrite plus the missing int8 wrappers, NOT a superior normalization. Both differ from production golden 'switch(cVar3)' which requires the upstream jumptable guard normalization outside this fixture's scope.

status_note: Phase A diagnostic fixture for PTRSUB-SWITCH-CAST-RESIDUAL-0001. A normal runner exit of zero means both pinned byte streams were reproduced and every raw difference is one of the registered known_raw_differences; the fixture remains overall=MISMATCH until the apply-side gaps (PTRADD castOutput arm + implied retype, castInput double-cast guard, castInput constant arm, PTRADD undo preflight/opUndoPtradd, TypeOpIntAdd/arithmetic output tokens) are fixed in src and the pins are re-observed. The production golden for glob_set is switch(cVar3); reaching it additionally requires the upstream jumptable guard normalization which is outside this fixture's direct observation.
